messages:
anya: Heads-up — hit a regression where the runtime started picking a slower kernel mix for short sequences when KV cache hits are ~60%. Need a quick nsys capture recipe to show kernel transitions + NVTX markers. Anyone got a compact CLI that captures cuda,nvtx,osrt and keeps file size sane?
sam: +1. Use bracketed capture around a 20s window after warmup. warm up for ~30s off-trace to populate KV cache, then capture 15-25s. Example I use: 
```
nsys profile --output triage_{pid} --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --sample-interval=1ms --capture-range=bracket --capture-range-start=nvtx:CAP_START --capture-range-end=nvtx:CAP_END --force-overwrite --timeout 60000 \
  --sample=all 
```
Replace the NVTX markers with your client bracket. Keeps overall file small because bracketed.
mike: A couple notes: 1) prefer --sample-interval=0.5ms for short kernels, default 1ms misses microbursts. 2) If you suspect kernel selection bias, include OSRT so you can align host->device queues. 3) turn on CUPTI timeline if available.
jess: Also add `--sample-filtering=none` if you want raw sampling (we had debiasing hide rare kernels). For size: use `--capture-interval=100us` only for hotspot spans; otherwise stick to 0.5-1ms. If you do multi-GPU, add `--trace=osrt,cuda,nvtx` and `--nvlink` flags.
nsys-bot: Reminder: bracketed capture requires NVTX marks present in the trace. If missing, capture will fall back to full-process.
anya: Good call. Quick question on NVTX placement — should we bracket only the fastpath loop or include prefetch/warmup ops? I care about kernel switching once KV hits stabilize.
sam: Bracket the steady-state region only. Pattern: startup -> populate KV -> NVTX:CAP_START -> run 20-25s -> NVTX:CAP_END -> drain. That isolates the kernel mix.
mike: If you want to correlate batching heuristics, add NVTX tags for batch boundaries (`BATCH_START/END`) and log seq len and KV-hit% to stdout with `logger` NVTX strings. Then you can grep timeline for those markers.
jess: One more: use `nsys status --verbose` after capture to check missed events. And run one short smoke capture with `--duration=10s` to validate your flags before doing the long run.
anya: Thanks all — I'll add BATCH_START/END and try the 0.5ms window. Will post the capture file and a tiny kernel timeline snippet if it repros. :thumbsup:
